solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Conservative more impolite and less refined

explanation.surface: A Tory politician described as both ruder and coarser than his rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cruder is rougher and less polished, the comparative of crude.

clue.text: Emerge as some gentleman at Eton

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A public-school gentleman makes his appearance at Eton.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to issue or flow out from a source, so to come forth.

clue.text: Moderate and decent with ire controlled

indicators.note: controlled suggests the letters of the words are managed into a new order

explanation.surface: A mediator who stays fair-minded and keeps his anger in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moderate' looks like an adjective but is the verb: to act as go-between in a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: To moderate a dispute is to mediate, stepping in between the parties.

clue.text: River is dangerous with final change in direction

indicators.note: the last letter is a compass point, east, and it is swapped for another compass point, north

parts.note: severe can mean dangerous, as in a severe injury

explanation.surface: A warning that a river is hazardous where it bends at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with final change in direction' swaps the final E (east) of SEVERE for N (north).
explanation.definitionFit: The Severn is Britain's longest river, flowing through Wales and England to the Bristol Channel.

clue.text: Interruption affected us badly, adult admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so one letter is placed inside the other word

parts.note: to hit something is to affect it badly
A is the abbreviation for adult, as in film classification

explanation.surface: Something has gone wrong and broken our flow, with a grown-up involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' only colours 'affected' (hit hard); it is not an anagram signal, since the letters stay in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiatus is a pause or gap in a sequence, a break in continuity.

clue.text: Rake had a nice estate in Spain

indicators.note: to rake is to stir over and turn about, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A dissolute playboy owned a lovely property in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rake' poses as a womaniser but signals rearranging HAD A NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacienda is a large landed estate or ranch in Spain or Spanish America.

clue.text: Time when penny's found in old money turning up

indicators.note: in a down answer turning up means the letters are read from bottom to top
found in means placed inside another word

parts.note: the lira was the old Italian currency before the euro

explanation.surface: A moment when a coin turns up among some outdated currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' puts P into LIRA to give LIRPA, which 'turning up' reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: April is a month, a period of time in the calendar.

clue.text: Rebellion of superior prude cloaking wickedness

parts.note: U is used for upper-class or superior, as in U and non-U

indicators.note: cloaking means wrapping round, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: a prig is a priggish, self-righteous prude

explanation.surface: A self-righteous puritan hiding his own vice leads a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the old British label for upper-class usage, hence 'superior'; the inner step makes PRISING.
explanation.definitionFit: An uprising is a popular revolt against authority, a rebellion.

clue.text: Morse can go wrong in love affairs

indicators.note: go wrong suggests the letters going astray into a new order

explanation.surface: Inspector Morse's romantic entanglements always seem to end badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go wrong' rearranges MORSE and CAN; Morse is the fictional Oxford detective, famously unlucky in love.
explanation.definitionFit: Romances are love affairs, relationships of courtship and passion.

clue.text: Match officials given twenty rules devoid of content!

indicators.note: devoid of content means emptied, so only the first and last letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: Referees handed a set of twenty regulations with nothing in them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devoid of content' keeps only R and S, the first and last letters of 'rules'.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorers keep the official tally at a cricket match, so they count as match officials.

clue.text: Fellow attending church's social function

parts.note: Dan is a man's name, standing for any fellow
CE is the Church of England; the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: A man going along to a parish get-together.
explanation.definitionFit: A dance is a social event where people gather to dance.

clue.text: Arabs running wild may be this

definitions.text: Arabs running wild may be this

parts.words: Arabs running wild may be this
parts.note: Arabs here are Arab horses, and horses running loose have nobody on their backs

explanation.definitionFit: Arab horses galloping free have thrown or never had anyone mounted on them.

clue.text: The thing's in pieces with the top piece missing

indicators.note: in a down answer the top is the first letter, which is removed

explanation.surface: Something is shattered, its uppermost fragment lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with the top piece missing' drops the B, the first letter of BITS.
explanation.definitionFit: The contraction for it is stands for the thing is, a pronoun plus verb.

clue.text: Guarded two notes and a coin

parts.note: re is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone cautious with a couple of banknotes and a small coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' here are sol-fa notes, not banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Reticent means reserved and not revealing one's thoughts, so guarded.

clue.text: Animal burrowed with leg at front of garden

parts.note: on is the leg side in cricket

indicators.note: front of picks the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A creature digging, its leg poking out at the edge of the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is also called the on side, so 'leg' gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: The dugong is a marine mammal, a sea cow of the Indian Ocean.

clue.text: Shun a dame cruelly, lacking any feeling of guilt

indicators.note: cruelly suggests the letters are treated roughly and thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone who snubs a lady heartlessly and feels no remorse about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unashamed means feeling no shame or embarrassment for what one did.

clue.text: Hard old woman ensnaring number in Pacific port

indicators.note: ensnaring means trapping inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A tough elderly woman traps a figure in a Pacific harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Lulu is a woman's name; the number slips in after the O, between old and woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Honolulu is the capital of Hawaii and a major Pacific seaport.

clue.text: Fellow giving sign of approval on return

indicators.note: on return means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a nod is a sign of approval

explanation.surface: A colleague nodding his agreement as he comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on return' reads NOD backwards. A don is a fellow of an Oxford or Cambridge college.
explanation.definitionFit: A university fellow, especially at Oxford or Cambridge, is called a don.

clue.text: Amount put into very big speeches

indicators.note: put into means placed inside another word

parts.note: OS is the abbreviation for outsize, very big
a ration is a fixed amount

explanation.surface: A quantity inserted into some enormous addresses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put into' sets RATION inside OS, the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize.
explanation.definitionFit: Orations are formal public addresses, so speeches.

clue.text: Chief dismisses one bloke

indicators.note: dismisses means sends away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The boss sacks a single employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismisses' takes I out of MAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Man is an informal word for a bloke or chap.

clue.text: Busy person who manages to keep quiet

indicators.note: to keep means to hold inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a coper is someone who copes, who manages
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

explanation.surface: A hard-working individual who succeeds in staying silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Busy' is British slang for a police officer, not an adjective. 'to keep' puts P inside COPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Busy is northern British slang for a policeman, and copper is the familiar term for one.

clue.text: Land you once left heading north

indicators.note: in a down answer heading north means read upward, so backwards

parts.note: ye is the old form of you

explanation.surface: A field you once abandoned as you travelled north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading north' reverses YE plus L, YEL, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ley is a piece of land put down to grass for a time, grassland.

clue.text: Female doctor, one getting cross with rock musician

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A woman doctor gets angry at a rock star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like 'angry' but is the X shape. Jimi Hendrix was the American rock guitarist.
explanation.definitionFit: Jimi Hendrix was a celebrated American rock guitarist and singer.

clue.text: A German repeatedly imprisoning a good person, a brainbox

indicators.note: imprisoning means locking up inside, so one piece goes within another
repeatedly means the piece is taken twice

parts.note: ST stands for saint, a good person

explanation.surface: A German, again and again, locks up a virtuous person, a clever one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A German' is the German indefinite article; the saint sits between its two copies.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein's name is used for any genius, so a brainbox.

clue.text: Man is one? Yes and no!

definitions.text: Man is one? Yes and no!

parts.words: Man is one? Yes and no!
parts.note: the Isle of Man is a piece of land surrounded by sea, yet John Donne wrote that no man is one

explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is a sea-girt landmass, while Donne's famous line denies a man is one.

clue.text: Funny aunt about to show character

indicators.note: funny means odd, so the letters are made strange and rearranged

explanation.surface: An eccentric aunt is about to reveal her personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' makes NATU from the aunt; 'show' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's nature is their essential character or disposition.

clue.text: Wood, say, fashioned to make on-board supports

indicators.note: fashioned means made or shaped anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Timber, for instance, worked into structural props on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like an example marker but is the fodder; 'fashioned' turns it into AYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Forestays are ropes or wires supporting a ship's foremast, running forward to the bow.

clue.text: Drug joke engenders fit

parts.note: E is the street abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A gag about drugs brings on a seizure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' is the verb meaning to fit out, not a seizure.
explanation.definitionFit: To fit out a ship or person is to equip them with what they need.

clue.text: Inspection of passage, allowing anyone to see inside

indicators.note: inside means placed within another word

parts.note: an adit is a horizontal passage into a mine
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for all

explanation.surface: An examination of a corridor that lets everyone look in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts U, the British film rating open to all ages, within ADIT.
explanation.definitionFit: An audit is an official inspection, typically of accounts.

clue.text: Ill-used, getting no place at Oxford? The reverse

indicators.note: the reverse tells us to read the whole string backwards

parts.note: to be up is to be in residence at university, such as Oxford

explanation.surface: Someone badly treated after failing to win a place at Oxford, or the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The reverse' turns the string NOPUTUP backwards. Students are 'up' when in residence at Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: To be put-upon is to be taken advantage of, so ill-used.

clue.text: Trendy rioter on the rampage inside

indicators.note: on the rampage means running wild, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A fashionable rioter running amok indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' at the end is the definition, used as a noun, not a container signal; 'on the rampage' makes TERIOR.
explanation.definitionFit: The interior is the inside of something, as a noun.

clue.text: Odd matter that creates a commotion

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange
pus is the matter from an infected wound

explanation.surface: Strange stuff that causes uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'matter' means the yellow matter of an infection, PUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumpus is a noisy disturbance, a commotion.
